about: Five behaviours of the agent clients that Slate's packaging could lean on, each checked hands-on before Slate relies on it. A behaviour stays unconfirmed until someone runs its check on the real client and records the result here (status, the date, the client's version and what was seen, plus as_checked when the check ran differently from its text); an unconfirmed one says exactly what's left (what_is_left). tests/packaging/test_packaging_client_behaviours.py holds this record complete and holds Slate to relying on none of the unconfirmed ones.

behaviours.what: OpenClaw expands Claude Code's plugin path placeholder (${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}) inside a Claude bundle's .mcp.json. Its bundle docs only cover ${PLUGIN_ROOT} for Agent Plugins bundles.
behaviours.how_slate_avoids_it: The plugin's MCP configs start the installed `slate` command by name and name no path, so no placeholder needs expanding.
behaviours.evidence: In a scratch OpenClaw home (OPENCLAW_HOME, OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR and OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH in a scratch folder, its own gateway port), `openclaw plugins install ./scratch-bundle --force --accept-capabilities` installed a Claude bundle (format bundle, bundleFormat claude, one mcpServers capability) whose .mcp.json runs `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/bin/echo-args --root ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}`. One `openclaw agent --local` turn on that home, with a model provider pointed at a dead loopback port, started the server before its model call: OpenClaw's own log line reads `[bundle-mcp] failed to start server "echo-args" (<home>/extensions/scratch-bundle/bin/echo-args --root <home>/extensions/scratch-bundle (cwd=<home>/extensions/scratch-bundle))`, and echo-args itself recorded the same command line. Expanded in the command and its arguments ('failed' only because echo-args isn't a real MCP server). ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json and its extensions were never touched (checksum and listing).
behaviours.as_checked: The behaviour's check with one change: the server's command line came from a local agent turn on the scratch home rather than a gateway started on it, because bundle MCP servers start per agent session, not at gateway start.
behaviours.check: On a throwaway OpenClaw state folder (OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR pointing at a temporary folder, never the real one), install a scratch Claude bundle whose .mcp.json runs `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/bin/echo-args` with `openclaw plugins install ./scratch-bundle`, start the gateway on that state folder, and read the server's command line in its logs: expanded to the bundle's folder, or the literal placeholder.

behaviours.what: Codex reads a Claude-style .claude-plugin/marketplace.json whose plugin sources are plain relative strings ("./plugins/slate"), not only its own {"source": "local", "path": ...} objects.
behaviours.how_slate_avoids_it: Codex gets Slate from the installer (skills linked into ~/.agents/skills, `codex mcp add slate -- slate mcp`); the plugin README says reading this repository as Codex's marketplace isn't confirmed.
behaviours.evidence: With a scratch CODEX_HOME (empty at the start), `codex plugin marketplace add` on a copy of the repository's .claude-plugin/ and plugins/ registered a local marketplace named slate, `codex plugin add slate@slate` installed slate 0.1.0 from the plain relative source "./plugins/slate", and `codex plugin list` shows `slate@slate installed, enabled 0.1.0 <copy>/plugins/slate`, the relative source resolved against the marketplace root. The installed copy holds all ten skills. Same on both builds; ~/.codex/config.toml byte-identical and ~/.codex's listing unchanged.
behaviours.check: With a scratch CODEX_HOME (never ~/.codex), add a local copy of the repository as a plugin marketplace with `codex plugin`, then list the marketplace's plugins: slate listed with its skills, or an error about the source.

behaviours.what: A nested `metadata.openclaw` block in SKILL.md frontmatter survives `skills-ref validate` and a claude.ai upload (the Agent Skills spec says metadata maps names to strings).
behaviours.how_slate_avoids_it: Slate's skills carry only name and description in their frontmatter, and `slate skills build` refuses metadata that isn't one level of strings.
behaviours.check: Run `skills-ref validate` on a scratch skill whose frontmatter nests `metadata: {openclaw: {requires: {bins: [slate]}}}`, then upload the same zip on claude.ai (Customize, Skills) by hand: accepted, or refused with which error.
behaviours.what_is_left: `skills-ref` isn't installed on this Mac, and installing it is a download nobody approved for this task. Then: `skills-ref validate` on a scratch skill whose frontmatter nests `metadata: {openclaw: {requires: {bins: [slate]}}}`, and the same skill's zip uploaded on claude.ai (Customize, Skills) by hand: accepted, or which error. Slate relies on neither.

behaviours.what: `claude plugin validate` accepts a plugin folder that holds both Claude Code's manifest (.claude-plugin/plugin.json) and an Agent Plugins manifest (plugin.json) at its root.
behaviours.evidence: `claude plugin validate --strict --json` on a copy of the built plugin folder (both manifests, and .mcp.json with Slate's server and the two hosted connectors) exited 0 with no errors, warnings or notes; it validated .claude-plugin/plugin.json and left the root plugin.json alone. The repository's marketplace (.claude-plugin/marketplace.json) validated the same way.
behaviours.check: `claude plugin validate --strict --json plugins/slate` and `claude plugin validate --strict --json .` from the checkout (or `slate skills build --check`, which runs the first wherever `claude` is installed).

behaviours.what: Which state folder the OpenClaw gateway uses. It decides whether OpenClaw sees the skills in ~/.agents/skills, which it reads only from its default state folder.
behaviours.evidence: `slate doctor --json --context openclaw-gateway`, run through the gateway in the phase-1 doctor spike at 04:49, saw OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR unset (the default state folder) and all 10 of Slate's skills in ~/.agents/skills, once each (its agents.skills.openclaw row, green).
behaviours.check: Run `slate doctor --json --context openclaw-gateway` through the gateway and read the agents.skills.openclaw row's state_dir and missing lists; `slate doctor` turns yellow when a gateway uses another state folder.
